lines.text: Three seconds earlier, it saw everything.
Watch the green boxes. Three objects tracked.
Cameras need contrast. Water takes it.
LiDAR fires a laser and times the echo. But a raindrop echoes too. The car sees a ghost point three meters ahead, and the real car behind it fades.
Fog is worse. In one fog chamber test, detection dropped by half.
Engineers do not fix one sensor. They add sensors that fail differently.
Radar passes through fog. But in heavy rain, it gains little.
A laser at fifteen fifty nanometers is allowed more power, so more signal survives.
Thermal cameras read heat, so warm bodies still stand out.
And coatings, air puffers, and wipers keep every lens clear.
Same storm. The driver sees a white wall. The car sees three objects.
Would you trust it with only one sensor?
